newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, fx swaps hold steady in late dealings.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, fx swaps hold steady in late dealings.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were stable in late dealings on Friday, but ecu/drachma traded a little lower after early ecu sales for drachmas, dealers said.

"Swaps and interbank deposits are stable in late trade," a state bank dealer said. "The market is long drachmas, and liquidity has increased because sales of two-year zero coupon bonds and 12-month T-bills amounting to 407 billion drachmas ($1.5 billion) were less than expiries of 500 billion last week."
Greece's February ice inflation fell to 6.6 percent year-on-year from January's 6.8 percent.
The central bank's intervention rate in overnight money was unchanged at 11.90 percent.
"Bonds were steady, and the day was quiet," a state bank bond dealer said.
The mark was quoted at 157.05/15 from Friday's 157.115 fix, the dollar at 269.35/45 drachmas from 269.350 and the Ecu at 305.74/84 from 305.490 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is trading at 305.37-42. It had opened at 305.45-50 but fell after small sales of ecus for drachmas by foreign investors in the morning," a foreign bank forex dealer said.
Its daily low was 305.33-38, and its range was between 305.38-55 on Friday, the dealer said.
